To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the composition control of low-volatilility compounds is possible by means of selective chemical vapor transport, provided that the sample composition is defined by the temperature of the source (charge), the composition of the source and the temperature of the sample.

the composition of a low-volatility solid compound can be controlled by reversible chemical vapor transport, in which one component is introduced into the compound from the vapor phase, and the second component is removed from the compound into the vapor phase.

composition control of low-volatitude solids can be achieved using chemical vapor transport reactions, and the composition is determined by the thermodynamic properties of the low-volatililty solid, the vapor, and the charge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of novel materials, the control of their composition (nonstoichiomety), and the study of their physical properties.
the development of a new approach for the control of composition in low-volatility compounds using reversible selective chemical transport.
the development of new methods for controlling the composition of solid compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the composition of a solid sample in a closed chemical-vapor-transport system is determined by the temperature and chemical composition of the charge (x1, T1).
the composition of a low-volatility solid can be controlled by reversible selective chemical vapor-transport reactions, provided a suitable vapor-transport system is employed.
the composition control of low-volativity inorganic solids is a feasible and promising method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the composition of a sample can be controlled in a closed system by the choice of appropriate values of T1, x1, and T1.

the composition of low-volatililty compounds can be controlled by the selective chemical vapor transport, provided the following conditions are satisfied: the charge and the sample should be placed in a closed system, and the temperature of the sample should be higher than the temperature of the charge.

composition control through chemical vapor transport can be achieved in a closed system if the following conditions are met: (1) the system is in the steady-state condition, (2) the sample composition is in the metastable region, (3) the vapor composition (x1) is fixed, and (4) the temperature of the sample is higher than that of the charge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the composition of low-volatitude solids can be controlled by adjusting the source temperature and composition.
the composition of a solid phase can be controlled by chemical vapor transport, provided the following three conditions are fulfilled.
